biggestGap: Nothing in the frame goes to black — cut the global ambient hard and clamp every flame light's range so its contribution dies inside ~2m, so the colonnade and ceiling fall off into true black a few metres back instead of being evenly grazed and legible right across the frame (fracDeepShadow 0.104 vs 0.331).
critiqueDetail: I correctly identified the film as panel B, high confidence, essentially instantly. Round 1's fix landed — the flames now emit light and warmFraction has gone 0.076 to 0.149 against a reference of 0.104, so they overshot rather than undershot — but that light has no range limit, so in our panel the entire back colonnade is uniformly washed and readable from floor to top of frame, while in the film the piers dissolve into pure black a couple of metres behind the ranks and the ceiling is a total void. The blacks are actually worse than round 1: fracDeepShadow fell from 0.135 to 0.104 against a reference of 0.331, and medianLuminance is 0.122 vs 0.086 — a flat lifted floor with no vignette. The knock-on is that all that spilled fill is also too blue and too vivid (meanLitHueDeg 255.9 vs 223.6, meanSaturation 0.294 vs 0.242), and the flames themselves read as ~25 identical teardrop billboards with no per-flame variation in size, colour temperature or flicker.
metrics: fracDeepShadow 0.104 vs 0.331 (-0.228); coolFraction 0.445 vs 0.324 (+0.121); medianLuminance 0.122 vs 0.086 (+0.035); meanLitHueDeg 255.9 vs 223.6 (+32.3); meanSaturation 0.294 vs 0.242 (+0.052); warmFraction 0.149 vs 0.104 (+0.045); fracShadow 0.497 vs 0.633 (-0.136); histogramEntropy 6.82 vs 5.95 (+0.87)

history.gap: Flames are self-luminous sprites that emit no light — no warm pools, no uplight, no falloff — leaving one uniform cold ambient that also lifts the blacks (fracDeepShadow 0.135 vs 0.331).

Flames now emit light but with unbounded range, and the global ambient is still too high, so nothing reaches black — the whole colonnade is evenly lit to the top of frame and fracDeepShadow fell further to 0.104 vs 0.331.
